item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00286","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C16","C06","C09"],"selected_candidate_label":"C16","confidence":0.82,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C16 plausibly supplied a material template for the child’s treatment of a commemorative observance centered on constitutional liberty. Both directives move from the historical significance of the Constitution and citizens’ rights to an operative appeal for observance by governmental, religious, civic, and educational bodies, followed by a call to renew commitment to the principles embodied in the Constitution. C06 and C09 share narrower elements—appeals to schools, churches, and civic groups, and the connection between Korea, communist aggression, and the defense of freedom—but neither matches the child’s central commemorative and constitutional structure as closely.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"it is fitting that this anniversary should be observed by our schools, our churches, our labor unions, and our religious, educational, and civic organizations of all kinds","parent_excerpt":"I also urge Federal, State, and local officials, as well as patriotic, religious, civic, educational, and other interested organizations, to arrange for appropriate ceremonies on Citizenship Day","explanation":"Both enumerate substantially the same institutional constituencies and enlist them in observing a civic commemoration."},{"child_excerpt":"celebrate December 10, 1952, by studying the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the Constitution of the United States ... and by giving thanks for the priceless heritage of liberty embodied in these great documents","parent_excerpt":"both native-born and naturalized citizens may have a fuller understanding of their rights and privileges and of their obligations and responsibilities as citizens of the United States","explanation":"The operative observance in each directive is framed as public education about constitutional rights, privileges, and civic responsibilities."},{"child_excerpt":"renew our determination that here in our own land the great guarantees in our Bills of Rights shall not be lost or weakened or curtailed","parent_excerpt":"renew and reaffirm on that day their faith in the principles and ideals embodied in the Constitution - the foundation of our strength and the symbol of freedom and justice for all","explanation":"The concluding exhortations share a distinctive renewal formula tied to constitutional principles, freedom, and justice."}]}
